commit.message:
lntest/unittest: start bitcoind conn after it syncs to the miner

In this commit, we fix a flake in TestFilteredChainView's bitcoind
polling subtests. NewBitcoindBackend used to start the chain connection
before bitcoind had synced to the miner. In RPC polling mode the
connection polls from bitcoind's height at start (0), so it replays
every historical block afterwards. Under load the replay can still be
running when the chain view registers its client. The replay of the old
tip (equal to the client's best block) is treated as a reorg, which
queues a disconnected event ahead of the connected events. The block
event queue is strictly ordered and nothing reads DisconnectedBlocks
in these tests, so the queue stalls and the filtered block never
arrives.

We now wait for the bitcoind RPC to be reachable, connect it to the
miner and sync, and only then create and start the connection, so the
poller starts at the synced tip and there is nothing to replay.

funding: fix flaky TestFundingManager{CustomChannelParameters,MaxPendingChannels}

In this commit, we fix two independent races in the funding manager
test harness that made these tests fail in CI.

TestFundingManagerCustomChannelParameters read Bob's initial forwarding
policy as soon as it had received his FundingSigned message. Bob sends
that message before he stores the policy, so the read could return
"channel not found". Bob emits the pending open event only after the
policy is stored, so the test now waits for that event first.

TestFundingManagerMaxPendingChannels has several channels waiting on
confirmation at once, but the mock notifier handed every registration
the same one-conf channel. Whichever goroutine received a confirmation
was arbitrary, so it could get the confirmation carrying another
channel's funding tx, fail validation, and never send ChannelReady. The
mock notifier can now route one-conf registrations by funding txid, and
this test confirms each tx on its own channel. Other tests keep the
shared channel.

commit.message:
pool: fix flaky TestConcreteRecyclePoolTests

In this commit, we fix a flake in testRecyclePool, which failed with
"original item not found" on a loaded CI runner.

GCQueue.Take hands out a freshly allocated item when the queue manager
goroutine does not answer within one millisecond. The test allowed only
two takes, so a single stalled take (common under -race or -cover with
parallel packages) used up an attempt without consuming the queued
original, and the test gave up even though the returned item was still
in the queue.

The pool only promises best-effort reuse, so we now take until the
original item is delivered. A timed-out take does not remove anything
from the queue, so the original is always reached. We also use gc and
expiry intervals of a minute so that the original cannot expire while
the test runs, and drop the one millisecond sleep that only masked the
scheduling dependence. The cleanliness assertion on the original is
unchanged.

commit.message:
ci: pre-pull the Postgres images the test fixtures need

In this commit, we pull the Postgres images the database test fixtures
use before the test legs run, with a bounded retry.

The fixtures start their server through dockertest, which checks for the
image locally and only pulls when it is absent, so a cold runner makes
exactly one pull. That pull is subject to Docker Hub's anonymous rate
limit, and when it is refused the error arrives several frames deep in a
migration test as an API error rather than as an infrastructure refusal.
A run then reads as a stack of Postgres migration failures -- the whole
"could not resolve reference postgres:11: 429" family -- which looks
like a database problem and is nothing of the sort.

Pulling up front turns that into one failing step that names the rate
limit. The retry is deliberately bounded: three attempts with linear
backoff, then fail the job. It does not paper over a persistent outage,
it distinguishes a transient limit from a real one.

Both tags the repository ships are pulled, since sqldb/postgres_fixture.go
uses postgres:11 and sqldb/v2/postgres_fixture.go uses postgres:15.

htlcswitch: fail fast when hodl tests run without the dev tag

In this commit, we make the htlcswitch tests that depend on hodl flags
fail immediately with a clear message when run without `-tags=dev`.

The production hodl.Mask never reports a flag as active, so a test that
sets HodlMask and is run without the tag does not fail at the point of
the problem. TestSwitchDustForwarding, for example, waited about 20
seconds and then reported `got totalDust=0 mSAT, expectedDust=70000000
mSAT ... timeout checking dust`, which looks like a product bug. The
tag is always set by `make unit` and CI, so this only affects direct
`go test` invocations.

Two tests already carried an inline build.IsDevBuild check with a
malformed message. We replace both with a shared requireDevBuild helper
and apply it to the other three tests that set a hodl mask:
TestSwitchDustForwarding, TestChannelLinkCleanupSpuriousResponses and
TestPipelineSettle. The helper fails rather than skips, so a missing tag
can never turn into a silently passing run.

chancloser: register mock expectations before sending ChannelFlushed

In this commit, we fix a flake in the early_offer subtest of
TestRbfChannelFlushingTransitions. The test sent the ChannelFlushed
event and only afterwards, inside assertSingleRemoteRbfIteration,
registered the CreateCloseProposal, CompleteCooperativeClose,
MarkCoopBroadcasted and BroadcastTransaction expectations. The state
machine handles the cached early OfferReceivedEvent on its own
goroutine as soon as it sees the flush event, so it could call the mock
signer before the test goroutine had set the expectation. testify then
panics inside the state machine goroutine ("method call was unexpected"),
which takes down the whole package. This is what failed in CI with an
unexpected CreateCloseProposal at fee 10,100.

We now register the expectations before sending ChannelFlushed. The
assertSingleRemoteRbfIteration helper only registers them itself when it
is also the one sending the init event, which is the case for all of its
other callers.

commit.message:
itest: stop watch-only nodes before their signer

In this commit, we stop the watch-only node before harness cleanup.
Otherwise the harness can remove the signer TLS cert while the
watch-only health check is still running, which makes an otherwise
passing test exit with a remote-signer error.

config: recognize the renamed BOLT 12 migration

In this commit, we update the BOLT 12 config guard to recognize
000017_offers. The native SQL experiment builds include the migration,
but the stale name prevents nodes from starting with offers enabled. A
build-tagged test asserts that these builds accept the config.

scripts: wait for routes in the backwards compat test

In this commit, we refresh routing policies after channel announcements and poll for the route each test payment needs. Seeing all channel announcements does not mean a sender knows the directional policies. The payment still runs once and must settle.
